defects.quote: Match-going fans now spend an average of 14 minutes per game waiting for VAR checks.
Referees got along fine for 150 years without video, so the game never needed it.
defects.known_rebuttal: Longevity is not evidence of accuracy. Officials' error rates on key decisions were measurable and significant, high-profile mistakes such as Thierry Henry's handball against Ireland in 2009 decided qualification, and once every fan could watch broadcast replays, uncorrectable errors eroded trust in results more than review delays do.
